newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR halts aid for Rwandans after Zaire protest.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR halts aid for Rwandans after Zaire protest.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said it suspended relief work for thousands of Rwandan Hutus in eastern Zaire on Friday after Zaireans attacked its staff in a protest over the presence of the unwanted refugees.

It was the latest setback for the agency, which also had to delay an airlift of the first batch of refugees out of the rebel-controlled eastern town of Kisangani on Friday after local officials expressed fears it would spread cholera.

Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said UNHCR wanted security guarantees from the rebels before resuming aid for more than 80,000 Rwandan Hutus after hundreds of protesters prevented an aid convoy from disembarking from a river ferry on the way to camps.
"We want local authorities to calm down the local population and guarantee the safety of our staff," she said.
The protesters stopped the convoy, which included two Danish and four local UNHCR employees, hammered on their vehicles and blocked their way, O'Toole said. No one was hurt.
The aid workers, who later returned to Kisangani, were told by local officials that they could not go to the refugee camps unless they gave food to the local Zaireans, she added.

O'Toole said local tensions were whipped up by aggressive local radio broadcasts against the refugees and unconfirmed reports circulating in town that the refugees had killed a rebel or several local Zaireans.
Tension has been rising in the region since the murder of three Zaireans three weeks ago near the refugee site of Lula which local people blamed on the refugees, she added.
O'Toole said the situation in Kisangani was very tense, amid reports of looting at a World Food Programme warehouse in town.
But she said UNHCR had no plans to evacuate its 15 expatriate and 25 local staff from the city, which was captured by the rebels last month.
In Kisangani, the protesters told Reuters the refugees should move deeper into the jungle away from Zaire's third city.
"The Zairean population refuses to let the whites (aid officials) take food to the refugees because the refugees are killing local Zaireans," said boat operator Yenga Masomboye.
Also on Friday, UNHCR was forced to delay an operation to airlift the first batch of refugees out of Kisangani after rebel officials expressed fear that it could spread cholera.
More than a million Hutu refugees fled eastern Zaire camps last October and November at the start of a campaign by rebels to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Most refugees returned to Rwanda in November but hundreds of thousands more fled deeper into Zaire, among them members of the former Rwandan government army and extremist Interahamwe militia responsible for massacres in Rwanda's 1994 genocide of Tutsis.
Aid workers are nursing the refugees back to health, but UNHCR's plan to take them on trucks, planes and barges across the Zaire river back home has been repeatedly delayed amid rebel formalities.
